log: The `civ1-wonder:darwins-voyage` pending-effect handler was only registered inside the Darwin's Voyage `BuildingComplete` effect. A game loaded into a fresh worker never runs that effect, so discharging the last free research completion threw `UnknownHandlerError`. `started.ts` now exports `registerHandler` and calls it from `getRules`, as civ1-government does for revolutions.
The save test takes its handler from the rules rather than a hand-registered stub, and checks the last completion is granted after a load.

Each wonder rule repeated its own obsoleting-advance check, and two were wrong: the Great Library kept granting advances after University, and the Lighthouse only went obsolete when its owner discovered Magnetism.

`Rules/lib/obsolete.ts` now holds the one wonder-to-advance table, and `isObsolete` is true once any player has completed the advance. It's derived from research, so nothing new is saved. `cityHasWonder` and `playerHasWonder` take the research registry and ignore obsolete wonders, so the per-rule checks are gone. `pyramidsActive` and `research-complete` use the same table.
